subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack OAuth token rotation in the Slack plugin, and where should client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and recovered?
rationale: The request changes Slack secret persistence and active runtime auth behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the storage, redaction, migration, refresh ordering, and operator recovery model.

options.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Add Slack rotation behind the Slack plugin boundary with secure persistence, transactional refresh, status/doctor repair, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep OpenClaw on static Slack token inputs for now and document the external rotation workaround until maintainers want to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Build a generic credential-refresh seam first
options.body: Design a shared plugin credential-refresh contract, then implement Slack token rotation as one consumer of that contract.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Add Slack rotation behind the Slack plugin boundary with secure persistence, transactional refresh, status/doctor repair, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Slack runtime/config history among the likely owners and is the best available owner for the security and product choice.
